main_text.p: vidias, potentum fastidia: perrum pere per obluctantes factiones, per insidiantes dolos, per insultante repulsas : & placido sibi semper constante vultu, nec frangi, nec etiam ferari : Atqui ex his crescit dein-ceps historiis ac theatris digna se-ges : Nam eorum præcipuè in annalibus gesta lectorem pascunt, quos in altum suus labor & sudor evexêre : Suspendit legentis animum conatus anceps, abripitque & obtutum defigit expectatio ; at heroicus vigor, & obstinatus per dedignans arduū ascensus, favorem prolicit : & tandem optatus exitus demulcet & plausum ciet : Erigi-turque in spem, atque ad audendum sollicitatur animus : dum in via illa, quæ à plebe ad decus est, confragosâ licet & difficultatum sentibus horridâ, signantur nihilominus antecedentium vestigia, qui-

page.notes: Show-through text in the right margin is not transcribed. Line-end hyphens ("Erigi-", "auden-", "nihi-", "qui-") are printed hyphens. The word "vidias" begins a fragment carried over from the previous page. Some words at the right edge are partly cut off by the scan (e.g. "perrum[pere]", "etiam[ferari]", "se[ges]"); the reading follows the visible letters.
